---
title: "longitudinal mixed model"
author: "Caroline Wheeler"
date: "2024-07-09"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(nlme)
library(pass.lme)
library(EMAtools)
```

```{r}
x <- read.csv("../data/2024-07-02_irAE mouse weights-cleaned.csv") 
```

linear mixed model with only random intercept
```{r}
lmm.ri <- lme(weight ~ group*days, data = x, random = ~1 | mouse)

summary(lmm.ri)
```

linear mixed model with random intercept and random slope
```{r}
lmm.ri.rs <- lme(weight ~ group*days, data = x, random = ~ days | mouse)
summary(lmm.ri.rs)
```

The more complex model is significantly better per the pval - so random slopes and intercepts
```{r}
anova(lmm.ri, lmm.ri.rs)
```
try different correlation structures
```{r}
lmm1 <- lme(weight ~ group*days, data = x, random = ~ days | mouse, correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~1 | mouse))
lmm2 <- lme(weight ~ group*days, data = x, random = ~ days | mouse, correlation = corAR1(form = ~1 | mouse))
lmm3 <- lme(weight ~ group*days, data = x, random = ~ days | mouse, correlation = corExp(form = ~1 | mouse))
```

```{r}
anova(lmm.ri.rs, lmm1)
anova(lmm.ri.rs, lmm2)
anova(lmm.ri.rs, lmm3)
```

```{r}
anova(lmm3)
```
